title: How headphones erase noise
kicker: Sample visual · every layout and block
deck: They don't block the sound. They add a second sound that wipes the first one out.
shows: A sample using every layout and block: how active noise cancelling works, drawn as a cutaway, a scroll story and a comparison

art.alt: A large pair of headphones above a noise wave and its opposite.

thirty_seconds: A microphone hears the noise outside.
A chip plays the exact opposite wave.
The two cancel, so your ear gets near silence.

spreads.question: How can adding sound make things quieter?
spreads.headline: Two opposite waves add up to nothing.

art.caption: Waves are drawn to explain, not measured.
art.alt: A red noise wave, a blue opposite wave, and a nearly flat green line where they meet.

steps.title: Noise arrives
steps.text: Sound is a wave of pressure that pushes and pulls on your eardrum.

steps.title: The chip flips it
steps.text: Where the noise pushes, the speaker pulls, a split second later.

steps.title: They meet
steps.text: Push and pull cancel, so the wave nearly flattens.

steps.title: Quiet
steps.text: Your ear gets the leftovers, plus your music.

spreads.question: What is in the ear cup?
spreads.headline: Four small parts do all the work.
spreads.text: Pull one ear cup apart and the job of each layer is plain.

art.caption: A simplified layout, not one real product.
art.alt: An exploded view of an ear cup: shell, chip board, speaker and cushion.

notes.title: Speaker
notes.text: Plays your music and the opposite wave.

notes.title: Chip
notes.text: Works out the opposite wave in a blink.

notes.title: Shell and microphones
notes.text: Microphones on the outside hear the noise first.

spreads.question: Isn't a thick cushion enough?
spreads.headline: Foam stops voices. The chip stops the drone.

sides.title: Passive: blocking
sides.text: Good on high, sharp sounds. Heavy, low sounds pass through.

art.alt: A barrier flattens the voice wave but barely touches the bass wave.

sides.title: Active: cancelling
sides.text: Good on steady, low sounds. Sudden sounds get through.

art.alt: A chip flattens the bass wave and barely touches the voice wave.

spreads.question: How does each sound compare?
spreads.headline: These charts show each form, with made-up numbers.
spreads.text: Every number here carries an Example badge, because this page is a sample. Real visuals use sourced numbers.

art.alt: Example bars of noise reduction by sound.

spreads.question: Where does it shine?
spreads.headline: A plane cabin is the perfect job.
spreads.text: The engine drone is steady and low, exactly what the chip handles best.

art.alt: Rows of seats and windows in a plane cabin at night.
